sample_plan.subpopulation_description: U.S. residents aged 0–7 (age-distribution category 0–14), including infants and very young children whose needs and activities are caregiver-shaped; no independent leisure interests, reading, cooking, work, or public-opinion profile is imposed.
U.S. residents aged 8–14 (age-distribution category 0–14); this child/caregiver band leaves independent interests, reading, cooking, work, and public-opinion profiles open.
U.S. residents aged 15–17 (age-distribution category 15–24); retains the younger part of this age group without assigning adult education, marital, labor-force, or public-opinion profiles.
U.S. residents aged 18–24 (age-distribution category 15–24); adult opinions and habits remain open to the supplied alternatives, with weighted demographic choices retained.

U.S. residents aged 25–54 (age-distribution category 25–54), with little or interrupted formal schooling and compatible lower educational attainment; all other supplied demographic choices remain available.

U.S. residents aged 25–54 (age-distribution category 25–54), with advanced educational attainment and the supplied highly accomplished researcher or specialist learning profile; demographic options otherwise remain open.
U.S. residents aged 25–54 (age-distribution category 25–54), allocated a warm, cooperative, considerate personality profile; other personality dimensions and weighted demographics are not restricted.
U.S. residents aged 25–54 (age-distribution category 25–54), allocated the unusually cynical or antagonistic personality extreme; weighted demographics and political views remain unrestricted.

U.S. residents aged 25–54 (age-distribution category 25–54), allocated a strongly progressive political-belief profile; party affiliation and other demographic choices retain their supplied alternatives.

U.S. residents aged 25–54 (age-distribution category 25–54), allocated a strongly conservative political-belief profile; party affiliation and other demographic choices retain their supplied alternatives.

U.S. residents aged 25–54 (age-distribution category 25–54), allocated a strongly optimistic and encouraging general-attitude profile; no political, personality, or demographic category is inferred from it.
U.S. residents aged 25–54 (age-distribution category 25–54), allocated a persistently pessimistic general-attitude profile.
U.S. residents aged 25–54 (age-distribution category 25–54), allocated an open-minded and curious general-attitude profile.
U.S. residents aged 25–54 (age-distribution category 25–54), allocated the unusually hostile and closed-minded general-attitude extreme.

U.S. residents aged 25–54 (age-distribution category 25–54); this illustrative profile combines traditional home cooking, deliberate infrequent shopping, health-focused habits, openness to new products, local cultural influences, frequent travel, and an active lifestyle. Demographic choices remain weighted and unconstrained.

U.S. residents aged 25–54 (age-distribution category 25–54); this contrasting profile includes adventurous food tastes, frequent shopping, an indulgent and sedentary routine, resistance to product changes, global influences, and preference for home-based recreation.

U.S. residents aged 25–54 (age-distribution category 25–54); this profile contrasts bold, spicy food with in-store shopping, organic food preferences, cautious product evaluation, traditional cultural influences, adventurous trips, and minimalist living.

U.S. residents aged 25–54 (age-distribution category 25–54); this profile allows mild, simple flavors, online shopping, conventional health preferences, high novelty seeking, cosmopolitan cultural influences, and predictable comfortable travel.

U.S. residents aged 25–54 (age-distribution category 25–54); this profile includes vegetarian food, budget-conscious shopping, a rare harmful health extreme, familiar homogeneous cultural surroundings, and local outings.

U.S. residents aged 25–54 (age-distribution category 25–54); this profile includes fully plant-based food, extravagant shopping, chronic health needs, layered cultural influences, and travel avoidance.

U.S. residents aged 25–54 (age-distribution category 25–54); this profile includes meat-centered meals, brand-conscious shopping, limited opportunity for exercise, a trusted-recommendation approach to new products, and travel mainly for obligations.
U.S. residents aged 55–64 (age-distribution category 55–64); supplied weighted demographic alternatives are retained, with a varied health-and-wellness habit profile.
U.S. residents aged 55–64 (age-distribution category 55–64); supplied weighted demographic alternatives are retained, with varied stress-management and coping habits.
U.S. residents aged 65–110 (age-distribution category 65 and older); the full supplied age range is retained, with varied stress-coping habits and no advanced-education restriction.
U.S. residents aged 65–110 (age-distribution category 65 and older); the supplied weighted demographics and broad attainment range are retained, alongside inconsistent wellness routines.
